turns.content: A rare mouse breast-cancer cell population shows low expression of a tumor-suppressor gene, and epigenetic silencing is suspected. Design a study that directly tests whether cytosine methylation at this locus differs between the cancer cells and matched healthy breast cells.

Distinguish what bulk RNA sequencing measures from what a locus-specific DNA-methylation assay measures. Which readout addresses the candidate epigenetic mark itself rather than only its expression consequence?
Choose a method that maps cytosine methylation at the tumor-suppressor locus with base-level resolution, and explain the chemical distinction on which its readout depends.
Design the matched comparison using the cancer cells and healthy breast cells. Specify the locus-level output to compare and how a methylation difference would be interpreted.
Why would Ras overexpression, bulk RNA sequencing alone, or knockout of a testis-specific DNA methyltransferase fail to provide the same direct test of methylation at this locus?

Suppose the cancer cells show higher methylation at the tumor-suppressor locus. What would that association support, and why would it not by itself prove that methylation is the unique cause of low expression?
What experimental controls and follow-up perturbation could strengthen the causal interpretation while keeping the locus-specific methylation comparison as the primary assay?
Give the recommended assay and matched-sample design, then state clearly what a positive differential-methylation result would and would not establish.
